def-indicator-function-of-closed-convex-:
## Definition

For any set $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, its extended-real indicator is
$$\iota_C(x)=\begin{cases}0,&x\in C,\\+\infty,&x\notin C.\end{cases}$$
def-proper-closed-convex-function-on-rn:
## Definition

Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and let $g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]$. Its effective domain is $\operatorname{dom}g=\{x:g(x)<+\infty\}$. The function is **proper** if $\operatorname{dom}g\ne\varnothing$; it is **convex** if
$$g((1-\theta)x+\theta y)\le(1-\theta)g(x)+\theta g(y)\qquad(x,y\in\mathbb R^n,\ 0\le\theta\le1),$$
using the endpoint convention $0\cdot(+\infty)=0$ of [[def-convex-and-strictly-convex-functionals-on-a-banach-space]]. It is **closed** (equivalently, lower semicontinuous in the extended-real convex-analysis convention used here) if its epigraph
$$\operatorname{epi}g=\{(x,s)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R:g(x)\le s\}$$
is closed in $\mathbb R^{n+1}$. The proximal-gradient items on this page assume $g$ is proper, closed and convex.

This page's closed-epigraph convention is explicit: it does not silently use an equivalence between sequential lower semicontinuity and topological closedness that would require an additional choice principle in the library's generic sequential convention. In finite dimensions this is the standard closed proper convex input to proximal algorithms.
lem-l-smoothness-descent-inequality:
## Statement

Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be continuously differentiable and suppose $\nabla f$ is Lipschitz with constant $L\ge0$ in the Euclidean norm. Then
$$f(y)\le f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle+\frac{L}{2}\|y-x\|_2^2\qquad(x,y\in\mathbb R^n).$$
def-extended-real-epsilon-subdifferentia:
## Definition

Let $g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper and convex in the convention of [[def-proper-closed-convex-function-on-rn]]. For $x\in\operatorname{dom}g$ and $\eta\ge0$, define
$$\partial_\eta g(x)=\{p\in\mathbb R^n:g(z)\ge g(x)+\langle p,z-x\rangle-\eta\text{ for every }z\in\mathbb R^n\}.$$
Write $\partial g(x)=\partial_0g(x)$. If $x\notin\operatorname{dom}g$, set $\partial_\eta g(x)=\varnothing$. When $g$ is finite-valued on a convex domain, $\partial g(x)$ agrees with [[def-subgradient-and-subdifferential]].
def-proximal-mapping:
## Definition

Let $g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper, closed and convex, and let $t>0$. For $v\in\mathbb R^n$, define the set-valued proximal mapping
$$\operatorname{prox}_{tg}(v)=\left\{u\in\mathbb R^n:g(u)+\frac{\|u-v\|_2^2}{2t}\le g(w)+\frac{\|w-v\|_2^2}{2t}\text{ for every }w\in\mathbb R^n\right\}.$$
The existence and uniqueness theorem on this page proves that this set is a singleton for every admissible $g,t,v$; its unique member is also denoted $\operatorname{prox}_{tg}(v)$.
def-strong-convex-composite-objective:
## Definition

Let $F:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be a proper convex extended-real function ([[def-extended-reals]]). For $\mu>0$, say that $F$ is **$\mu$-strongly convex** if for every $x,y\in\operatorname{dom}F$ and $0<\theta<1$,
$$F((1-\theta)x+\theta y)\le(1-\theta)F(x)+\theta F(y)-\frac\mu2\theta(1-\theta)\|x-y\|_2^2.$$
This definition permits $F$ to be extended-real-valued outside its effective domain. The endpoint cases are identities and are not included in the strict range for $\theta$.
lem-proper-closed-convex-function-affine:
## Statement

Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and let $g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper, closed and convex in the epigraph convention of [[def-proper-closed-convex-function-on-rn]]. Then there are $a\in\mathbb R^n$ and $b\in\mathbb R$ such that
$$g(x)\ge\langle a,x\rangle+b\qquad(x\in\mathbb R^n).$$
lem-smooth-composite-sum-preserves-prope:
## Statement

Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be continuous and convex, and let $g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper, closed and convex under the epigraph convention of [[def-proper-closed-convex-function-on-rn]]. Then $F=f+g$ is proper, closed and convex in the same convention.
lem-prox-indicator-is-euclidean-projecti:
## Statement

Let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be nonempty, closed and convex. Its indicator $\iota_C$ is proper, closed and convex in the convention of [[def-proper-closed-convex-function-on-rn]]. For every $t>0$ and $v\in\mathbb R^n$, $\operatorname{prox}_{t\iota_C}(v)$ is the singleton consisting of the unique nearest point in $C$ to $v$.
thm-proximal-operator-existence-resolven:
## Statement

Let $g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper, closed and convex in the epigraph convention of [[def-proper-closed-convex-function-on-rn]]. For every $t>0$ and $v\in\mathbb R^n$, the set $\operatorname{prox}_{tg}(v)$ is a singleton. Its unique element $u$ satisfies the resolvent equivalence
$$u=\operatorname{prox}_{tg}(v)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (v-u)/t\in\partial g(u).$$
For any $v_1,v_2$ and $u_i=\operatorname{prox}_{tg}(v_i)$,
$$\|u_1-u_2\|_2^2\le\langle u_1-u_2,v_1-v_2\rangle.$$
In particular the proximal map is nonexpansive.
def-proximal-gradient-mapping:
## Definition

Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be continuously differentiable with $L$-Lipschitz gradient for some $L>0$, and let $g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper, closed and convex. Define
$$T_L(x):=\operatorname{prox}_{g/L}\!\left(x-\frac1L\nabla f(x)\right),\qquad G_L(x):=L(x-T_L(x)).$$
The proximal theorem [[thm-proximal-operator-existence-resolvent-firm-nonexpansive]] ensures the point $T_L(x)$ is uniquely defined. For a nonempty closed convex set $C$ and $g=\iota_C$, the projected-gradient update is
$$T_L^C(x)=P_C\!\left(x-\frac1L\nabla f(x)\right),\qquad G_L^C(x)=L(x-T_L^C(x)),$$
where $P_C$ denotes the unique nearest-point projection; this equality follows from [[lem-prox-indicator-is-euclidean-projection]].
lem-prox-l1-is-soft-thresholding:
## Statement

For $n\ge1$, $\lambda>0$, $t>0$, and $v\in\mathbb R^n$,
$$\operatorname{prox}_{t\lambda\|\cdot\|_1}(v)=\big(S_{t\lambda}(v_i)\big)_{i=1}^n,$$
where $S_\tau$ is the soft-thresholding map of [[def-soft-thresholding-function]].
lem-proximal-three-point-inequality:
## Statement

Let $g$ be proper, closed and convex, let $L>0$, let $f$ be differentiable at $y$, and set $x^+=\operatorname{prox}_{g/L}(y-\nabla f(y)/L)$. For every $z\in\mathbb R^n$,
$$g(x^+)+\langle\nabla f(y),x^+-y\rangle+\frac{L}{2}\|x^+-y\|_2^2+\frac{L}{2}\|x^+-z\|_2^2\le g(z)+\langle\nabla f(y),z-y\rangle+\frac{L}{2}\|z-y\|_2^2.$$
alg-proximal-gradient-and-fista:
## Definition

Assume $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ is convex and continuously differentiable with $L$-Lipschitz gradient, $L>0$, and $g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ is proper, closed and convex. For a finite iteration budget $N\ge1$, initial point $x_0\in\mathbb R^n$, and exact evaluations of $T_L$ from [[def-proximal-gradient-mapping]], the proximal-gradient mode returns
$$x_k=T_L(x_{k-1}),\qquad k=1,\ldots,N.$$

The FISTA mode sets $t_1=1$, $y_1=x_0$, and for $k=1,\ldots,N$ computes
$$x_k=T_L(y_k),\qquad t_{k+1}=\frac{1+\sqrt{1+4t_k^2}}2,\qquad y_{k+1}=x_k+\frac{t_k-1}{t_{k+1}}(x_k-x_{k-1}).$$
It returns $x_N$. A fixed-period restart with period $m\in\mathbb N$, $m\ge1$, runs this FISTA recurrence for at most $m$ updates per block and, after each full block, resets $t_1=1$, $y_1$ to the block's last iterate, and the previous iterate to that same point. A final shorter block stops at the budget. Each call uses the exact proximal point; no inexact call is covered by this algorithm definition. The finite budget makes the output a finite iterate even when no convergence or monotonicity of consecutive accelerated objective values is asserted.
lem-proximal-gradient-one-step-estimate:
## Statement

Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be convex and continuously differentiable with $L$-Lipschitz gradient, $L>0$, and let $g$ be proper, closed and convex. Put $F=f+g$ and $x^+=T_L(y)$. For every $z\in\mathbb R^n$,
$$F(z)-F(x^+)\ge\frac{L}{2}\|x^+-y\|_2^2+L\langle y-z,x^+-y\rangle.$$
thm-projected-gradient-fixed-point-kkt-c:
## Statement

Let $C=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ Gx\le d\}$ be a nonempty polyhedron and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be convex and continuously differentiable with $L$-Lipschitz gradient, $L>0$. For $x\in C$, the projected-gradient mapping of [[def-proximal-gradient-mapping]] satisfies
$$G_L^C(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad-\nabla f(x)\in N_C(x),$$
where $N_C$ has the outward convention of [[def-kkt-residual-and-normal-cone]]. If a feasible tuple $(x_*,\nu,\lambda)$ satisfies $\lambda\ge0$, $\nabla f(x_*)+A^T\nu+G^T\lambda=0$, and $\lambda_i((Gx_*-d)_i)=0$ for every inequality, then $x_*$ is such a fixed point and is a global minimizer over $C$. The converse to this KKT-multiplier implication is not asserted.
alg-certified-inexact-proximal-gradient-:
## Definition

Use the finite proximal-gradient or FISTA recurrences of [[alg-proximal-gradient-and-fista]], but replace each exact proximal output $x_k=T_L(y_k)$ by a reported finite point $x_k\in\operatorname{dom}g$ and certificate
$$L(y_k-x_k)-\nabla f(y_k)\in\partial_{\eta_k}g(x_k),\qquad \eta_k\ge0,$$
where $\partial_{\eta}g$ is defined in [[def-extended-real-epsilon-subdifferential]]. In proximal-gradient mode $y_k=x_{k-1}$; in FISTA mode use the same momentum update as the exact recurrence. If the certificate cannot be supplied for a call, return status **inconclusive** and make no convergence claim for that run. The inexact rate theorems on this page use this certificate itself; they do not assert rates for an unverified objective-gap tolerance alone. For $\eta_k=0$ the resolvent theorem [[thm-proximal-operator-existence-resolvent-firm-nonexpansive]] makes the certificate equivalent to an exact proximal call.
lem-fista-energy-estimate-sequence:
## Statement

Let $F=f+g$ satisfy the exact FISTA hypotheses of [[alg-proximal-gradient-and-fista]], and suppose $x_*$ minimizes $F$. Use its iterates $x_k,y_k,t_k$ and set $t_0=0$, $u_0=x_0-x_*$, and
$$u_k=t_kx_k-(t_k-1)x_{k-1}-x_*\qquad(k\ge1).$$
Then for every $k\ge1$,
$$\frac{2t_k^2}{L}\bigl(F(x_k)-F(x_*)\bigr)+\|u_k\|_2^2\le\frac{2t_{k-1}^2}{L}\bigl(F(x_{k-1})-F(x_*)\bigr)+\|u_{k-1}\|_2^2,$$
where the $k=1$ right-hand objective term is interpreted as zero.
thm-proximal-gradient-o1k-objective-boun:
## Statement

Under the exact proximal-gradient hypotheses of [[alg-proximal-gradient-and-fista]], suppose $F=f+g$ has a minimizer $x_*$. From any $x_0\in\mathbb R^n$, the iterates $x_k=T_L(x_{k-1})$ satisfy
$$0\le F(x_k)-F(x_*)\le\frac{L\|x_0-x_*\|_2^2}{2k}\qquad(k\ge1).$$
lem-inexact-proximal-gradient-one-step-e:
## Statement

Let $f$ be convex, continuously differentiable and have $L$-Lipschitz gradient, $L>0$, and let $g$ be proper, closed and convex. Given $y$, suppose $x^+$ and $\eta\ge0$ satisfy
$$L(y-x^+)-\nabla f(y)\in\partial_\eta g(x^+).$$
With $F=f+g$, for every $z\in\mathbb R^n$,
$$F(z)-F(x^+)\ge\frac{L}{2}\|x^+-y\|_2^2+L\langle y-z,x^+-y\rangle-\eta.$$
thm-fista-o1k2-objective-bound:
## Statement

Under the exact FISTA hypotheses of [[alg-proximal-gradient-and-fista]], suppose $F=f+g$ has a minimizer $x_*$. For every $x_0\in\mathbb R^n$ and $k\ge1$,
$$0\le F(x_k)-F(x_*)\le\frac{2L\|x_0-x_*\|_2^2}{(k+1)^2}.$$
lem-inexact-fista-energy-estimate:
## Statement

Let $x_k,y_k,t_k$ be the certified inexact FISTA iterates of [[alg-certified-inexact-proximal-gradient-and-fista]], with errors $\eta_k\ge0$, and let $x_*$ minimize $F=f+g$. Set $t_0=0$, $u_0=x_0-x_*$, and $u_k=t_kx_k-(t_k-1)x_{k-1}-x_*$. Then
$$\frac{2t_k^2}{L}(F(x_k)-F(x_*))+\|u_k\|_2^2\le\frac{2t_{k-1}^2}{L}(F(x_{k-1})-F(x_*))+\|u_{k-1}\|_2^2+\frac{2t_k^2}{L}\eta_k,$$
with the $k=1$ previous objective term interpreted as zero.
thm-inexact-proximal-gradient-summable-e:
## Statement

Under the inexact proximal-gradient model of [[alg-certified-inexact-proximal-gradient-and-fista]], suppose $F=f+g$ has a minimizer $x_*$ and let $\eta_k\ge0$ be the certified errors. Then for every $N\ge1$,
$$\min_{1\le k\le N}\bigl(F(x_k)-F(x_*)\bigr)\le\frac{L\|x_0-x_*\|_2^2/2+\sum_{k=1}^N\eta_k}{N}.$$
If $\sum_{k=1}^\infty\eta_k<\infty$, then $F(x_k)-F(x_*)\to0$. This gives a best-iterate bound; no last-iterate $O(1/k)$ rate is asserted.
thm-strong-convex-proximal-gradient-and-:
## Statement

Assume the exact algorithm hypotheses of [[alg-proximal-gradient-and-fista]], that $F=f+g$ is $\mu$-strongly convex for $\mu>0$ under [[def-strong-convex-composite-objective]], that a minimizer $x_*$ exists, and that $F(x_0)<+\infty$. Exact proximal gradient satisfies
$$F(x_k)-F(x_*)\le q^k(F(x_0)-F(x_*)),\qquad q=\frac1{1+\mu/(4L)}<1.$$
For fixed-period restarted FISTA with $m=\lceil\sqrt{8L/\mu}\rceil$ updates per full block, the restart-point gaps obey
$$F(x_{jm})-F(x_*)\le2^{-j}(F(x_0)-F(x_*)),\qquad j\ge0.$$
thm-inexact-fista-weighted-error-bound:
## Statement

Under the certified inexact FISTA model of [[alg-certified-inexact-proximal-gradient-and-fista]], suppose $F=f+g$ has a minimizer $x_*$. For each $k\ge1$,
$$F(x_k)-F(x_*)\le\frac{2L}{(k+1)^2}\left(\|x_0-x_*\|_2^2+\frac2L\sum_{j=1}^k j^2\eta_j\right).$$
In particular, weighted summability $\sum_{j\ge1}j^2\eta_j<\infty$ preserves an $O(1/k^2)$ objective bound under this certificate model.
